text:
priya: Heads-up — running into an ambiguity with per-route logging + inspect-unmask UX. TL;DR: high-throughput routes are sampling logs down, but the console 'inspect' unmask is returning full user email for some tenants. Need decision: hash-by-default vs remove entirely when sampled out.

michael: oof. can you paste an example? is this only the console unmask or also in the ephemeral debug blob?

priya: Example (sanitized):
```
Request { route: "/v1/generate", tenant: "acct-123", body: { prompt: "..." }, headers: { Authorization: "Bearer ..." } }
Logged sample: request.user_email = "alice@example.com" (visible in inspect)
```
But for sampled telemetry we only keep partial context. When a route is in 'high-volume' mode we do dynamic sampling and sometimes the console's inspect button shows the raw email (bad).

sam: We should avoid raw PII in any sampled telemetry. Proposal: three-tier redaction config per-route: `remove`, `hash:hmac-sha256:tenant-salt`, `mask:partial`. Default for sampled data = `hash`. Full inspect (unmasked) must require audit token and separate retention.

jess: love the three-tier idea. two followups: 1) who rotates the tenant-salt, 2) how do we show this in dashboard so support can triage without asking legal?

kevin: salty detail: HMAC with per-tenant salt is fine but affects dedup/embedding lookup for PII detection. If you hash, downstream deduping won't match unhashed copies we keep in secure vault for legal audits. Need mapping table (hashed -> sealed blob id) guarded by ACL.

priya: agreed. proposed flow: sampled logs use `hash` (tenant-salt), console inspect requires `inspect:unmask` audit token; when unmasking we fetch sealed blob id and return value in ephemeral view (no raw in logs). This keeps logs PII-free.

leah: UX note: let's add an infobar when inspect returns unmasked values: "Viewing ephemeral unmasked data — access logged and audited" and a one-click download of audit record. ops wants that for SOC traces.

michael: operational constraints: hashing for every request adds CPU. For high-throughput routes we already offload to inference GPUs and minimal CPU. Could we do hashing asynchronously after sampling decision? i.e., log sample pointer immediately, schedule redaction/hashing job to populate the sample blob.

sam: that works but increases tail latency for the 'inspect-able' entry. If unmask is requested before job completes, we should show "pending audit blob" and queue a higher-priority job.

jess: console/dashboard question — telemetry team: can we surface a new column in per-route traffic dashboard: "pct sampled (redacted)" + "avg time to unmask blob (s)"? Product wants SLA numbers before enabling on a few top tenants.

kevin: quota/billing concern: creating audit blobs and mapping tables is storage+ops cost. We need a toggle per-tenant that gates whether we create sealed blobs for them. For tenants opting out, we must default to `remove` not `hash`.

priya: action items I hear: 1) default sampled-data behavior = `hash` (HMAC-SHA256 + per-tenant salt). 2) unmasking path uses audit token + sealed blob mapping (no raw PII in logs). 3) console UX shows clear audit banner + download. 4) telemetry adds two KPI columns. 5) provide opt-out which flips default to `remove`. 6) implement async hashing job with priority bump on unmask.

leah: + add rollout plan: canary to 5% of tenants, only on non-chat routes first. add feature-flag in console for support teams.

ops-bot: deploy-bot: New sampler-redact v2 scheduled to canary in eng-platform on 2024-08-18 02:00 UTC (automated).

michael: one more legal check — retention for sealed blobs: default 90d but must be configurable by tenant and tracked in billing. also we need a retention purge job.

priya: I'll draft an RFC w/ sequence diagrams and quick PR for the console banner. I'll include cost estimates for audit blobs. Assigning owners: sampling runtime = sam, console + UX = leah + jess, telemetry columns = michael, operations gating + mapping tables = kevin.

sam: ok will prototype hash hook and async job. expected perf hit: ~2% CPU on control plane during canary.

jess: I'll mockup banner and audit download.

priya: thanks. if no objections I'll open RFC + canary PR tomorrow. :+1:

kevin: +1 from me.

michael: +1, ping legal for retention ok.

priya: filing RFC now.
